facts: This appeal by special leave is directed against a judgment of the Allahabad High Court confirming the conviction of the appellants for offences u/ss. 302 and 325 read with S. 149 of the Indian Penal Code as also for some less serious offences.
The detailed facts of the case have been given in the judgment of the Sessions Judge and that of the High Court and it is not necessary for us to repeat the same.

It is true that the High Court has rejected a good part of the prosecution case regarding the motive or the actual cause of the occurrence but it has accepted the main details of the occurrence which resulted in injuries to three persons and death of two others.
The appeal being by special leave we can interfere only if we find that there is some gross violation of any principle of law or a serious miscarriage of justice.
petitioner_arguments: Mr. Goyal appearing for the appellants submitted that having disbelieved the essential details of the prosecution case, the High Court ought not to have convicted the appellants but should have acquitted all the accused.

The standard adopted by the High Court was that where an accused was shown to have taken part in the assault armed with a weapon which actually caused injuries to the prosecution witnesses or the deceased he was to be convicted.
court_reasoning: Having gone through the judgment of the High Court which is a well-reasoned one and has considered all the aspects of the prosecution case, we find ourselves in complete agreement therewith.

The fact of the matter is that none of the appellants had received any injuries and the High Court merely conjectured that they might have received injuries as a result of the blows given by some of the prosecution witnesses.
holding: Accordingly, we find no merit in the appeal which is dismissed.
